about.bio:
I am a Ph.D. candidate in the Department of History of Science at Example University, where I study how scientific instruments shaped nineteenth-century ideas about the natural world. My dissertation traces the circulation of astronomical photographs between observatories, museums, and the popular press.

Before graduate school I worked as a research assistant at a natural history museum and studied physics as an undergraduate. My writing has appeared in academic journals as well as a few general-audience outlets. I am always happy to talk with students, journalists, and fellow researchers.
